searchText: <@!708771937983397898> the explorer had issues right around the merge, that could explain it... I noticed that, it seemed like it re-synced a few times. It was showing those blocks before though. but then over night a few days ago my misses went from 19 to 85, days after the merge actually happened and now I see a bunch missing from epoch 911-985 base fee on goerli is only 7 -- I think 2-4 hours until the shadow fork merge? It shouldn't take long to get the base fee up right 1266 difficulty left. is the difficulty of a goerli block ( 1 vs 2) random? It can 10x every ~5 minutes, so in 10 minutes it should be sufficient. Semi-random. If Clique is working properly is should always be 2, but Görli has exposed a number of problems with Clique (and there's some rather poor implementations that don't help), plus some validators are often often. All of which leads to a lot of out of turn blocks with a difficulty of 1. So not really random, but still pretty unpredictable. I think it is worth making sure the beacon explorer is 100% merge ready too as that's one of the primary ways people will judge if the merge is successful (whether or not it's correct) Hi I'm getting a 503 @ https://explorer.goerlishadowfork.ethdevops.io/ is this expected? ty guessing <10 min to it next block!? looks like (shadowfork goerli) beaconchain site hasn't updated in the last 12 minutes https://goerli.etherscan.io/block/6596856 ttd 9692860 reached 10 minutes ago doesn't seem like any of the proposed blocks the explorer is showing have any execution data also seems like besu has been the only one to be part of the graffiti after the ttd -- which is the last 30+ minutes Ahhh Frens keep up the strong work! My blind basic guess is that 1) either just frontend thing 2) **if not**, just shadowforkmerge (new dictionary term?) growing pains (config? peering/networking issues?) and well worth it (not sure if it has been done before) -- hopefully some basic config changes would fix this (if 1) is not the case) 🙂 I don't want to come off as a a whining spectator but perhaps that is all I am. Sorry to flood the channel. I'll look for updates later. ^ just waking up so I've only got preliminary info. Goerli shadow fork was a success, chain is finalizing and healthy proposal numbers. I forgot to add a jwt secret to node connected to the beaconexplorer, so everything just crashed when it tried to use the engine api(oops). This just happened because the explorer runs on the bootnode and I tend to set up bootnodes manually. It's been fixed now, but the remnant of the forgetfullnes exists in the missing attestation+proposals from when the node was down. I'll rebuild that db in a bit. I'll update everyone with a more detailed split about client performance, etc after I'm properly awake 😅 Looks like we went down from 99.6% participation to ~85%, not too bad considering we have mainnet split and far higher load than previous testnets. I think some clients already said they knew things that might break. I'll see if there were unexpected issues. Nice! does anyone here other than Marius (no offense buddy, you're busy) have experience with `mege-fuzz`? I am a go newbie and I can't seem to make it work correctly. If so, details are in <#956608253465346168>

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: Semi-random.  If Clique is working properly is should always be 2, but Görli has exposed a number of problems with Clique (and there's some rather poor implementations that don't help), plus some validators are often often.  All of which leads to a lot of out of turn blocks with a difficulty of 1.

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: So not really random, but still pretty unpredictable.
